title: The plus construction computes sheafification
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf of sets on $\mathcal C$. For an object $U$, define $\mathcal F^+(U)$ to be the equivalence classes of pairs consisting of a covering $\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ and sections $s_i\in\mathcal F(U_i)$ whose pullbacks agree after passing to a covering of each $U_i\times_UU_j$, where two pairs are equivalent when they have a common covering refinement on which the sections agree; restrictions are obtained by pullback of coverings and sections. Put $\mathcal F^{++}=(\mathcal F^+)^+$. The Sites Theorem Tag 00WB (theorem-plus) says: (1) $\mathcal F^+$ is separated and the canonical map $\mathcal F^+\to\mathcal F^{++}$ is injective, as in [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-plus-separated]; (2) $\mathcal F^{++}$ is a sheaf; and (3) the canonical map $\mathcal F\to\mathcal F^{++}$ is a sheafification. More precisely, if $\theta:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F^\#$ is the universal-property sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], there is a unique isomorphism $\mathcal F^{++}\simeq\mathcal F^\#$ over $\mathcal F$, carrying the canonical map to $\theta$.

source.place: Sites, Theorem Tag 00WB (theorem-plus), parts (1)--(4), with the plus construction of Section 7.10

mathlib_searches.query: plus construction of a presheaf on a Grothendieck site is separated, its double plus is a sheaf, and the map to double plus is sheafification
mathlib_searches.results: CategoryTheory.presheafToSheaf and plusPlusAdjunction describe Mathlib sheafification, but no declaration packages the Sites 00WB plus-construction theorem for arbitrary sites

mathlib_searches.query: presheaf F plus plus sheaf separated sheafification universal property
mathlib_searches.results: Presieve.IsSheafFor, CategoryTheory.Sheaf.isSheafFor, and sheafificationAdjunction are available; no theorem identifies an explicit F++ with the universal-property sheafification
plusPlusAdjunction gives an abstract adjunction in the concrete sheafification construction, but no arbitrary-site 00WB statement with the separatedness and canonical-map clauses
Mathlib contains the sheafification adjunction and IsSheafFor criteria, but no explicit plus-construction separatedness theorem or F -> F++ comparison isomorphism for a general site
